title: Biological Clocks: The Suprachiasmatic Nucleus & Circadian Rhythms
description: Explore circadian master pacemaking: SCN molecular clocks, retinohypothalamic blue light cues, and pineal melatonin synthesis.

slides.title: The Master Clock: Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN) ⏰
slides.content:
# The Internal 24-Hour Conductor

Nearly every physiological process in our bodies—body temperature, hormone release, blood pressure, alertness—oscillates in a roughly **24-hour cycle** known as a **circadian rhythm** (Latin: *circa* = about, *dies* = a day).

* **The Master Biological Pacemaker**: A tiny cluster of ~20,000 neurons located in the **Suprachiasmatic Nucleus (SCN)** of the anterior hypothalamus, perched directly above the optic chiasm.
* **Autonomous Molecular Oscillators**: Even when isolated in a culture dish, individual SCN neurons maintain a self-sustaining autonomous firing rhythm driven by transcription-translation feedback loops of clock genes (**CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, CRY**) cycling over approximately 24.2 hours!

slides.title: Zeitgebers & The Retinohypothalamic Tract ☀️
slides.content:
## Entraining to Solar Time

Because the human endogenous clock runs slightly longer than 24 hours (~24.2 hrs), it must be reset (entrained) daily by environmental time cues called **Zeitgebers** ('time-givers'), the most powerful of which is sunlight.

### The Blue Light Pathway:
1. A specialized subset of retinal cells called **Intrinsically Photosensitive Retinal Ganglion Cells (ipRGCs)** express the photopigment **melanopsin**.
2. ipRGCs do not process images; they detect diffuse ambient irradiance, responding maximally to **short-wavelength blue light (460-480 nm)**.
3. ipRGC axons travel along the **Retinohypothalamic Tract (RHT)** directly to the SCN, releasing glutamate to synchronize the internal clock.
4. **Pineal Gland & Melatonin**: The SCN projects multi-synaptic inhibitory signals to the pineal gland during daylight. When darkness falls, SCN inhibition ceases, allowing the pineal gland to synthesize and surge **Melatonin** into circulation, opening the 'sleep gate'!

quizData.question: Which photopigment in retinal ganglion cells mediates circadian entrainment by detecting ambient blue light?
quizData.explanation: Melanopsin is expressed in intrinsically photosensitive retinal ganglion cells (ipRGCs) and responds directly to blue light to entrain the SCN master clock.
